speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Education regarding the reported erratum for an "A" Level Chemistry exam paper on 16 November 2022 (a) when and how was the error in the exam paper discovered; (b) how were the schools alerted and what was the timeline; (c) what guidance is provided to schools on communicating examination errata and whether affected students should receive extra time; and (d) how will unexpected circumstances that arise during exams be considered in a marking process.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: asked the Minister for Education whether he can provide an update on the "errata" during the recent GCE "A" Level Chemistry examination where there were differing practices across institutions such that certain schools were given extra time from five to 15 minutes to check and correct whilst others not given additional time.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: During the examination, a few schools sought additional clarifications on the erratum with the Singapore Examinations and Assessment Board (SEAB).

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: This would ensure that students continue to have the full duration of two hours to complete the paper.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have Clementi residents who read the news of this and were concerned.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: First, can the Minister of State share why these errata are happening and is it more often?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: On the second one, the exam paper and the erratum were prepared by Cambridge Assessment International Education.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Both the exam paper as well as the erratum were printed and issued together to every student at the start of the exam.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, basically, it is not a common incident.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: For each case, we do seek to be fair to all students.
